models.sample_description: Firm-year observations from the COMPUSTAT Global Industrial and Commercial file, 1996–2004. The sample requires fully consolidated audited observations with nonmissing dependent and independent variables, retains countries with investor-protection measures, and excludes Japan, South Korea, India, Pakistan, and financial institutions. It also removes the top and bottom 1 percent of abnormal accruals and observations with absolute studentized residuals greater than 3. At least three consecutive years of data are required to construct abnormal accruals, making 1996 the first test year.
models.method_details: The paper describes equation (1) as a fixed-effects model with year-specific dummies and two-digit-SIC industry dummies, but does not identify the underlying estimator from the allowed vocabulary.

dependent_variable.name: AB_ACCR
dependent_variable.definition: Signed abnormal accruals for firm i in year t, scaled by lagged total assets. The measure is actual total accruals less predicted total accruals. Total accruals are (earnings before extraordinary items − operating cash flows) / lagged total assets; earnings before extraordinary items are net income (#32) less extraordinary items (#33). Operating cash flows and current accruals are defined in the CFO entry. Predicted accruals are [sales_t × (current accruals_t−1 / sales_t−1) − gross PPE_t × (depreciation_t−1 / gross PPE_t−1)] / lagged total assets, where depreciation_t−1 is Compustat item #11 less item #13, with missing amortization item #13 set to zero; gross PPE is item #77 and lagged total assets item #89. Missing deferred-tax, untaxed-reserve, and minority-interest values used in operating cash flows are treated as zero. The construction is formula-based; the paper reports no fitted construction regression.
dependent_variable.formula: AB_ACCR_it = actual total accruals_it − predicted total accruals_it; actual total accruals_it = (earnings before extraordinary items_it − operating cash flows_it) / total assets_i,t−1; predicted total accruals_it = [sales_it × (current accruals_i,t−1 / sales_i,t−1) − gross PPE_it × ((D&A #11 − amortization #13)_i,t−1 / gross PPE_i,t−1)] / total assets_i,t−1.

dependent_variable.name: AB_ACCR
dependent_variable.definition: Signed abnormal accruals for firm i in year t, scaled by lagged total assets. The measure is actual total accruals less predicted total accruals. Predicted accruals are [sales_t × (current accruals_t−1 / sales_t−1) − gross PPE_t × (depreciation_t−1 / gross PPE_t−1)] / lagged total assets, where depreciation_t−1 is Compustat item #11 less item #13, with missing amortization item #13 set to zero; gross PPE is item #77 and lagged total assets item #89. evidence.quote: La Porta et al. (1998) develop what they
The sixpoint index

This index is based on six specific elements of investor protection dealing with the
ability of outside (minority) investors to challenge the control of the firm by managers
and dominant (inside) owners. Country-level scores can range from 0 to 6 based on the
sum of six indicator variables that reflect shareholder rights: (a) the ability to vote by
mail, (b) the ability to gain control of shares during the shareholders’ meeting, (c) the
possibility of cumulative voting for directors, (d) the ease of calling an extraordinary
shareholders’ meeting, (e) the availability of mechanisms allowing minority
shareholders to make legal claims against directors, and (f) shareholders have
preemptive rights that can be waived only by a shareholders’ vote. Larger values of the
antidirector rights’ index indicate that minority shareholders are better protected
against expropriation by management and controlling shareholders.

dependent_variable.name: AB_ACCR
dependent_variable.definition: Signed abnormal accruals for firm i in year t, scaled by lagged total assets. The measure is actual total accruals less predicted total accruals. Total accruals are (earnings before extraordinary items − operating cash flows) / lagged total assets; earnings before extraordinary items are net income (#32) less extraordinary items (#33). Operating cash flows and current accruals are defined in the CFO entry. Predicted accruals are [sales_t × (current accruals_t−1 / sales_t−1) − gross PPE_t × (depreciation_t−1 / gross PPE_t−1)] / lagged total assets, where depreciation_t−1 is Compustat item #11 less item #13, with missing amortization item #13 set to zero; gross PPE is item #77 and lagged total assets item #89. Missing deferred-tax, untaxed-reserve, and minority-interest values used in operating cash flows are treated as zero. The construction is formula-based; the paper reports no fitted construction regression.
dependent_variable.formula: AB_ACCR_it = actual total accruals_it − predicted total accruals_it; actual total accruals_it = (earnings before extraordinary items_it − operating cash flows_it) / total assets_i,t−1; predicted total accruals_it = [sales_it × (current accruals_i,t−1 / sales_i,t−1) − gross PPE_it × ((D&A #11 − amortization #13)_i,t−1 / gross PPE_i,t−1)] / total assets_i,t−1.

dependent_variable.name: AB_ACCR
dependent_variable.definition: Signed abnormal accruals for firm i in year t, scaled by lagged total assets. The measure is actual total accruals less predicted total accruals. Total accruals are (earnings before extraordinary items − operating cash flows) / lagged total assets; earnings before extraordinary items are net income (#32) less extraordinary items (#33). Operating cash flows and current accruals are defined in the CFO entry. Predicted accruals are [sales_t × (current accruals_t−1 / sales_t−1) − gross PPE_t × (depreciation_t−1 / gross PPE_t−1)] / lagged total assets, where depreciation_t−1 is Compustat item #11 less item #13, with missing amortization item #13 set to zero; gross PPE is item #77 and lagged total assets item #89. Missing deferred-tax, untaxed-reserve, and minority-interest values used in operating cash flows are treated as zero. The construction is formula-based; the paper reports no fitted construction regression.
dependent_variable.formula: AB_ACCR_it = actual total accruals_it − predicted total accruals_it; actual total accruals_it = (earnings before extraordinary items_it − operating cash flows_it) / total assets_i,t−1; predicted total accruals_it = [sales_it × (current accruals_i,t−1 / sales_i,t−1) − gross PPE_it × ((D&A #11 − amortization #13)_i,t−1 / gross PPE_i,t−1)] / total assets_i,t−1.

dependent_variable.name: AB_ACCR
dependent_variable.definition: Signed abnormal accruals for firm i in year t, scaled by lagged total assets. The measure is actual total accruals less predicted total accruals. Total accruals are (earnings before extraordinary items − operating cash flows) / lagged total assets; earnings before extraordinary items are net income (#32) less extraordinary items (#33). Operating cash flows and current accruals are defined in the CFO entry. Predicted accruals are [sales_t × (current accruals_t−1 / sales_t−1) − gross PPE_t × (depreciation_t−1 / gross PPE_t−1)] / lagged total assets, where depreciation_t−1 is Compustat item #11 less item #13, with missing amortization item #13 set to zero; gross PPE is item #77 and lagged total assets item #89. Missing deferred-tax, untaxed-reserve, and minority-interest values used in operating cash flows are treated as zero. The construction is formula-based; the paper reports no fitted construction regression.
dependent_variable.formula: AB_ACCR_it = actual total accruals_it − predicted total accruals_it; actual total accruals_it = (earnings before extraordinary items_it − operating cash flows_it) / total assets_i,t−1; predicted total accruals_it = [sales_it × (current accruals_i,t−1 / sales_i,t−1) − gross PPE_it × ((D&A #11 − amortization #13)_i,t−1 / gross PPE_i,t−1)] / total assets_i,t−1.

evidence.quote: La Porta et al. (1998) develop what they
The sixpoint index

This index is based on six specific elements of investor protection dealing with the
ability of outside (minority) investors to challenge the control of the firm by managers
and dominant (inside) owners. Country-level scores can range from 0 to 6 based on the
sum of six indicator variables that reflect shareholder rights: (a) the ability to vote by
mail, (b) the ability to gain control of shares during the shareholders’ meeting, (c) the
possibility of cumulative voting for directors, (d) the ease of calling an extraordinary
shareholders’ meeting, (e) the availability of mechanisms allowing minority
shareholders to make legal claims against directors, and (f) shareholders have
preemptive rights that can be waived only by a shareholders’ vote. Larger values of the
antidirector rights’ index indicate that minority shareholders are better protected
against expropriation by management and controlling shareholders.

independent_variables.name: INVPRO (ANTI_DIR)
independent_variables.definition: Country-level six-point antidirector-rights index, scored from 0 to 6 as the sum of six indicator variables for shareholder rights: ability to vote by mail; ability to gain control of shares during shareholders’ meetings; cumulative voting for directors; ease of calling an extraordinary shareholders’ meeting; mechanisms for minority shareholders to make legal claims against directors; and preemptive rights that can be waived only by a shareholders’ vote. Higher scores indicate stronger minority-shareholder protection.
independent_variables.formula: sum of six 0/1 shareholder-rights indicators; range 0–6.

evidence.quote: La Porta et al. (1998) develop what they
The sixpoint index

This index is based on six specific elements of investor protection dealing with the
ability of outside (minority) investors to challenge the control of the firm by managers
and dominant (inside) owners. Country-level scores can range from 0 to 6 based on the
sum of six indicator variables that reflect shareholder rights: (a) the ability to vote by
mail, (b) the ability to gain control of shares during the shareholders’ meeting, (c) the
possibility of cumulative voting for directors, (d) the ease of calling an extraordinary
shareholders’ meeting, (e) the availability of mechanisms allowing minority
shareholders to make legal claims against directors, and (f) shareholders have
preemptive rights that can be waived only by a shareholders’ vote. Larger values of the
antidirector rights’ index indicate that minority shareholders are better protected
against expropriation by management and controlling shareholders.

It requires fully consolidated audited observations with nonmissing dependent and independent variables, retains countries with investor-protection measures, and excludes Japan, South Korea, India, Pakistan, and financial institutions. It also removes the top and bottom 1 percent of annual returns and earnings per share before extraordinary items and observations with absolute studentized residuals greater than 3. The sample requires at least two consecutive years of data, making 1995 the first test year; the earnings-conservatism analysis is smaller because it requires additional stock-return data.
models.method_details: The paper describes the Basu earnings-conservatism framework and reports robust t-statistics, but does not identify the underlying regression estimator.

review_notes: Selected the paper’s three stated earnings-quality analyses as the principal full-sample regression families: signed abnormal accruals (equation 1/Table 4), loss reporting (equation 2/Table 5), and earnings conservatism (equation 3/Table 6). The introduction names these three outcomes, and the research-design/results sections test each against investor-protection proxies; each table reports five proxy-specific full specifications. This is a substantive earnings-quality study, not a method-development paper.

The signed abnormal-accrual measure is computed by the paper’s reported formula from prior-year ratios and accounting items; no fitted construction regression is reported, so no supporting regression dependency is added. Later separate Big 4 and non-Big 4 sample partitions described after Table 6 are follow-up partitions and are excluded from the principal family.

The supplied reading text renders equation operators in equations (1)–(3) as hyphens, while visual inspection of physical PDF pages 14, 16, and 17 confirms plus signs; equation_text uses the printed PDF notation and quotations remain literal to the supplied reading.

Equation (3) prints MB*DR for both β25 and β26, but Table 6 reports MB*DR and MB*R as separate coefficient rows. The equation text preserves the printed duplicate; the 27-term RHS inventory follows Table 6, and the discrepancy is flagged for review.
Equation (2) prints P(LOSS=1) equal to a linear predictor while Table 5 labels the models logistic regression. The equation is preserved as printed, and no inverse-logit link is added.

Footnote 5 specifies all six ANTI_DIR rights and the 0–6 score; footnotes 6, 8, and 9 clarify the analysis windows and missing-value handling for depreciation and operating cash flows. Footnote 10 says country-clustered Rogers t-statistics use 42 country degrees of freedom, whereas Table 5 reports asymptotic z-statistics; this inference discrepancy is preserved for review. The supplied reading text on page 31 is corrupted after the first footnote 6 sentences; the physical PDF page was inspected, and citations use only intact supplied text.

Table 6 is titled as an analysis of Big 4 clients, while the displayed five-proxy specifications include BIG4/non-BIG4 interaction terms and report n = 68,167; the printed title and values are retained.
